demand.reason: Global antimony consumption is estimated at roughly 110,000 metric tons annually, placing it within the high-demand band of 100,000–1,000,000 tons.

growth.reason: Demand is projected for moderate growth (6–12% CAGR), driven by military procurement spikes for ammunition and an emerging, high-capacity clean energy vector in antimony-based solid-state batteries (ASSBs) for utility storage.

supplier_concentration.reason:
Mining: China produced 40,000 of the 110,000 tons mined in 2025 (36%), followed by Russia (29%) and Tajikistan (20%), placing primary mining diversity in the 30–50% band (Score 2).


Refining: Downstream processing into antimony oxide and metal is heavily concentrated. China accounts for 70–80% of refined output, tracking securely within the concentrated 65–85% band (Score 4).

reserves.reason:
Time-frame: World reserves are more than 2 million tons (about 2.4 million tons summed across countries), roughly 20 years of supply at 2025 mine output of 110,000 tons, placing it in the 15–30 year band (Score 4).


Diversification: China holds about 35% of listed reserves (830,000 tons), followed by Russia (15%), Bolivia (13%) and Kyrgyzstan (11%); US reserves are 60,000 tons (the Stibnite project). The HHI is about 0.18, in the well-distributed band (0.15–0.25, Score 2).

end_use.reason:
Defense & National Security (+1.5): critical input for military antimonial lead ammunition, armor-piercing projectiles, and infrared sensors. Energy Generation & Grid (+1.5): functions as the primary chemical foundation for emerging grid-scale antimony energy storage batteries. Electrification & Transport (+0.5): used as antimonial lead in conventional automotive battery grid plates. Construction & Heavy Industry (+0.5): applied pervasively as a flame retardant in commercial building materials.


Sector presence scores total 4.0 across 4 qualifying sectors. The breadth bonus adds +1.5, yielding an objective composite score of 5.5.

substitutability_recyclability.reason:
Substitutability: Hydrated alumina and organic compounds function as commercially deployed substitutes in flame retardants, and alternative alloys compete in battery grids with minor trade-offs, matching Score 2.


Recyclability: Secondary recovery from lead smelters processing spent lead-acid automotive batteries is highly mature. Recycling loops routinely supply approximately 15% of demand, tracking within the low but non-trivial 5–20% recycling tier.

extraction_refining.reason: Antimony extraction relies on mature pyrometallurgical operations, including high-temperature roasting and smelting. The chemistry is well-documented, widely understood, and moderately complex without relying on exotic proprietary processes.

upcoming_projects.reason: The pipeline is adequate. Advanced brownfield restarts at Stibnite (USA) and Hillgrove (Australia), combined with major expansions via the Talco Gold JV in Tajikistan, are securely capable of adding 10–20% to supply within 3–5 years.

india_position.reason:
Import Dependence: India has no antimony mine output, but its smelters run on imported concentrate and India exports antimony metal, supplying 22% of US imports of unwrought antimony in 2021–24 (USGS). With no ore of its own but a refining base, India sits in the marginal domestic production band (Score 4).


Strategic Posture: Antimony is officially recognized on India's critical minerals list with customs duties exempted. However, lacking a dedicated KABIL mandate or foreign asset acquisitions, India's strategy reflects early-stage declared strategic intent (Score 3).

price_volatility.reason: Antimony prices experienced extreme market breakdown, rising from $5.31/lb in 2021 to about $25/lb in 2025 (USGS) after China's August 2024 export restrictions and its December 2024 ban on sales to the US (suspended in November 2025 until 27 November 2026). Weaponized supply constraints trigger Score 5.

capability.name: Antimony
capability.next_move: Turn Hindustan Zinc's by-product stream into metal and trioxide at scale; tie up concentrate for the smelters India already runs.
capability.what_india_has: Smelters that run on imported ore and concentrate (6,460 t in 2022-23) and export metal; Hindustan Zinc, which recovers antimony from smelter dust and slag as a by-product; high-purity antimony and antimony trioxide at the Nuclear Fuel Complex.
capability.cost: No public plant figure found. A new mine is costly: Perpetua's Stibnite gold-antimony project in Idaho is put at US$2.2 bn.

stages.india: No mine output. 255 kt of contained antimony in inferred resources: Himachal Pradesh (68%) and Madhya Pradesh.

stages.world: Roasting and smelting to metal and trioxide; China has 70 to 80% of refined output.
stages.india: Smelters process imported ore; India supplied 22% of US imports of unwrought antimony in 2021-24. Hindustan Zinc recovers trioxide of over 95% purity from slag.

stages.world: Antimony trioxide for flame retardants; antimonial lead for batteries.
stages.india: Exported 22,852 t of antimonial lead and 1,590 t of antimony alloys and scrap in 2022-23; the Nuclear Fuel Complex makes high-purity antimony.

stages.world: Flame retardants, lead-acid batteries, ammunition, solar glass.
